chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub from Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ibn Faddal from Ibn Bukayr from Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Abdillah said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about al-'azl (coitus interruptus), so he said, 'That is up to the man.'

key_terms.أَبَا عَبْدِ اللَّهِ: Abu Abdillah (Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq, peace be upon him)
key_terms.إِلَى الرَّجُلِ: Up to the man / The decision lies with the husband

ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on coitus interruptus (azl) and who has the authority to decide?
ai.summary: In this concise narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the right of *'azl* (coitus interruptus) is discretionary for the husband, reflecting the early Shia juristic view that it does not require the wife's explicit consent unless it causes her harm. This ruling underscores the husband's autonomy in marital intimacy while establishing the baseline for later scholarly debates on whether the wife's right to procreation or pleasure might limit this prerogative.
